💡 Key Takeaways
  • ‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ indicates Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics.
  • In a recent development, thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead.
  • The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ indicates Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics.

In a recent development, thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than won 3-2. The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before.

The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he mentioned, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 win at the Azteca Stadium and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards.

Recent findings suggest that against Mexico, the defender was sent off for a late tackle in the 54th minute with England 2-1 up. Against Spain, he contributed to Elliot Anderson being sent off in the 63rd minute with England 3-0 up. Quansah had his pocket picked by Lamine Yamal and Anderson’s attempt to chase back and rectify the situation ended with him fouling the winger.

It was not only a red card but a penalty; the prompt for Spain to launch a furious and hitherto unadvertised fightback. It had the stand that housed the press box shaking. Structural integrity was very much a theme.

Industry observers note that as in Mexico, Tuchel made defensive changes. This time, it was Myles Lewis-Skelly for Harry Kane; Djed Spence for Anthony Gordon. Tuchel also withdrew Jude Bellingham, who went off shaking his head. It was easy to understand his frustration. He was excellent. Tuchel had removed his two prime attackers. He also put Dan Burn on towards the end, albeit this time not as part of a back five. England stayed in a 4-4-1 formation, with Quansah moving from central defence to right-back. As in Mexico, the 10-man low block resisted.

Industry observers note that as much as Tuchel disagreed, this felt like Argentina reloaded as well. “No, not at all,” he noted, when the World Cup semi-final defeat was raised. “Because of one man down. We would not have been in this situation if it was 11 against 11.”.

Industry observers note that the parallels, nevertheless, were there. Tuchel made defensive substitutions at 1-0 up against Argentina; it was a back five on that occasion. As against Spain, his team could not get out and they faced a flurry of chances. There were other factors in play at the World Cup, chief among them the high levels of fatigue within the squad. England could not hold out, conceding two late goals to exit and bring down a wave of criticism on Tuchel.

Industry observers note that the score is the ultimate takeaway. It can skew analysis. Had Trafford not got back up after parrying a shot from the Spain substitute Fermín López to brilliantly repel Aymeric Laporte’s follow‑up, England would have gone from enjoying a fabulous result to stewing over an opportunity missed. The stakes were nowhere near as high as at the World Cup, but they would have gone from finishing top of their Nations League group to advancing into the quarter-finals as an unseeded second-place team.

In terms of Tuchel’s approach to the closing stages of a massive game, what changed?

The truth for England lay in the opening 63 minutes. This was where the evidence of a decisive shift could be found, the reasons for the swell of optimism. England have never played better under Tuchel – and this was against the team to beat; the world and European champions. On their turf.

It has been revealed that spain were without the injured Rodri and Dani Olmo, and Luis de la Fuente strangely decided to use Pedri only as a substitute, but their lineup still shimmered with menace; Lamine Yamal was frightening. Yet before their penalty, converted by Mikel Oyarzabal, they did not have a shot on target. Or a real chance.

Sources indicate that what stood out from the first whistle was England’s front‑foot intent; the bravery on the ball. They believed they would win and there was a fearlessness about them. They made forward moves on the half turn. There was a slickness about their combinations.

Spain have never suffered like this under De la Fuente and it was everything Tuchel had dreamed of when he started to plot a upcoming version of his team after the World Cup; a more fluid game model, a response to the Argentina defeat.

Tuchel loved England’s buildup play, which included some of Trafford’s passing. He loved the high press; the aggression in the duels; the threat on set pieces. He said he loved the low-block defending too. Ben White was excellent at right-back and there was a coming-of-age performance from Lewis Hall at left-back, but it felt wrong to single out individuals.

Sources indicate that “We didn’t stop and I think we are ready to go [like this] for 90 minutes,” Tuchel said. “It was a complete performance and we will not look back now. Go forward and stay hungry. We will not go back on this way of playing that we find ourselves since the World Cup.”.

It has been revealed that ezri Konsa, who headed in the second goal from a Declan Rice corner, remarked England “would have scored two more” if they had kept 11 men on the pitch. “You saw until the red card how much quality we had,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that “We dominated the game. The instruction was to keep going at them. Don’t stop. To keep our foot on the pedal. Argentina was different; different circumstances.”.

Industry observers note that tuchel was asked about the journey from the heartbreak of Argentina to this point; the end of a stirring Nations League group campaign, including the 7-0 win against Croatia in Rijeka. It has not all been super exciting; the 2-1 Wembley win against Croatia last Thursday, for example, was a grind. Was he always confident of a successful reboot?

“It took me a while to digest [the World Cup] and see the way forward,” he mentioned. “How we can help and adjust and improve? We had reviews and so on but the clarity came in the first Nations League camp [in September and October] with the players.

Recent findings suggest that “The first week was not so easy. Some players were still upset from the World Cup. Some were new in the team. Some had digested it, some had not. But it was notable to have this process together and everyone committed to wanting to improve in certain aspects of the game.

“We had the energy right to take the next steps and from there we went. Full credit to the players, how they buy in. It’s amazing that it came together like this now.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games, and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel.
  • It has been revealed that at Summer Game Fest 2026, we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again.
  • Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games, and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel.

It has been revealed that at Summer Game Fest 2026, we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong?

Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years.

Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2's pure survival horror to look forward to.

It has been revealed that rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason.

Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat.

This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running.

All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode.

At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away.

In a recent development, there are still some scares hiding in here, though, ready to make complacent players jump out of their seats. Special Xenomorphs have tricks to pounce on distracted players, throwing chaos into the middle of their carefully coordinated rain of fire. Others have the ability to spit from afar, breaking tight defenses that count on the Xenos' predictable tactics from other games and the movies.

Recent findings suggest that it's been 40 years since Aliens first graced the major screen, but Fireteam Elite 2 manages to refresh that mix of horror and action well enough, despite sharing much of its bones with the original game. But the disturbing lack of polish threatens to undo Cold Iron Studios' best ideas.

Those ideas include more varied enemies, which can disrupt almost any tried-and-tested team composition, and even a late-game class that rewards an extensive knowledge of the game by letting veterans pick weapons from all over the roster to create a custom loadout.

Sources indicate that these playful creative swings somewhat offset the frustration caused by glitched objectives, enemy AI that often goes off the rails, and performance issues that have often given me flashbacks to its predecessor's worst moments on PS4. Sometimes, you can just tell when six extra months would've done a game a lot of good, and it's obvious that Fireteam Elite 2 will be in a much better place by spring.

That said, its loose and confident approach to design is rare to see when dealing with games that adapt well-established IPs like Alien.

Recent Star Wars games have achieved just that, and even if Fireteam Elite 2 misses some of its shots and has faced more initial trouble than the USCM's first incursion on LV-426, it's safe to say its heart and mind are in the right place. No one can take that away from the devs. Show me another modern Alien video game that allows you to zap Xenomorphs to death with a major cannon or to hold them off with combat drones.

We've seen developers win uphill battles before, and we know for a fact the huge Alien fandom is as enduring as the deadly extraterrestrials, so Daybreak and Cold Iron have a chance to turn things around and solidify Fireteam Elite 2 as the iterative but satisfying sequel it actually is.

Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is available now for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. A Nintendo Switch 2 version is coming in 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France.

There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling.

According to recent reports, which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer. He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records.

In scoring his first under-21s goal, in the penultimate minute of regular time, Dowman eclipsed Jude Bellingham to become the team’s youngest scorer at 16 years and 320 days, three days after surpassing the Real Madrid midfielder’s record as the under-21s’ youngest player. Bellingham was almost four months older than Dowman when he scored his first goal for the age group, in September 2020. Bellingham made only four appearances for the under-21s, a result of being fast-tracked into the senior team, and Dowman could emulate him again, though he is expected to feature in next summer’s Under-21 European Championship in Albania and Serbia.

In a recent development, the common view from coaches and teammates, and something stressed by Lee Carsley, the under-21s head coach, is that it is easy to forget Dowman is six weeks shy of his 17th birthday. Against France, it was also extremely easy to overlook that this was Dowman’s first start for the under-21s, after a substitute appearance against Portugal last Friday. His first action set the tone on Monday, using his body to box off the ball then jinking up the right flank, zipping it through the legs of Dayann Methalie before skating forward and sending the Sunderland left-back juddering on to his backside.

Dowman exhibited plenty of neat touches, and a couple of effortless first-time passes, but those who have watched him develop say his work rate and willingness to do the other side of the game are among his biggest strengths.

“We look at Max and see how good he is on the ball, how attacking he is, but I thought he was outstanding off the ball,” Carsley stated, presumably thinking of the moment Dowman scampered deep into his own half to intercept a stray France pass. He was not finished after scoring either. At one point he had five blue shirts haring after him as he stormed into the France half and, seconds later, his quick feet lured the opposition captain, Nathan Zézé, into a foul on the edge of the France penalty area.

Dowman is among the next wave of players pushing to step up to Thomas Tuchel’s squad, perhaps at its forefront. It is a well-trodden path and the current crop need not look too far for inspiration. Elliot Anderson and Jarell Quansah, both of whom started England’s triumph at the last under-21 Euros in Bratislava, began Sunday’s memorable victory for the seniors in Madrid. Jobe Bellingham and Josh King are the latest players to make the transition into Tuchel’s squad and more will follow.

It has been revealed that jack Hinshelwood and Trey Nyoni, of Brighton and Liverpool respectively, impressed at the base of midfield and the 19-year-old Mikey Moore, another to score on his first start for the under-21s, shone down the left flank, opening the scoring. The Everton midfielder Harrison Armstrong entered as a substitute and supplied Dowman’s winner, and Armstrong’s clubmate Tyrique George also highlighted promise after replacing Moore. Archie Gray captained the under-21s against Portugal but did not feature on Monday, with Carsley revealing he has spoken to the Tottenham midfielder about Scotland wanting him to switch allegiance. “I just said to him: ‘Keep me in the picture, if it’s something that you were thinking of,’” Carsley said. “I think Archie is very connected to our pathway.”.

England’s budding talent is not confined to the under-21s. Carsley took a closer look at Brian Madjo, the imposing 17-year-old striker who scored on his Aston Villa debut in the Super Cup in August, the Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven and the West Brom forward Jimmy-Jay Morgan, who signed from Chelsea in the summer, before his squad departed for Bristol last week, the trio joining the under-21s for four days of training at St George’s Park.

Dowman, after two under-21 appearances comprising a little more than 120 minutes, is putting the squeeze on. “Max is doing something special for his age and he is pushing people a lot older than him,” mentioned Moore, who is on loan from Tottenham at Köln and hopes to face his idol Harry Kane and Bayern Munich on Friday. “He’s a top kid. You kind of forget how old he is. My little brother is 17 and he [Dowman] feels older to me than my little brother … He has been top and everywhere he goes, he just takes that next step.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HSBC’s top brass defended their strategy Monday to frustrated shareholders in the lender’s largest market, as Europe’s biggest bank continued to face calls to be split up.

At an informal shareholder meeting in Hong Kong, Chairman Mark Tucker and CEO Noel Quinn took questions from investors on complications ranging from how the bank was approaching demands for an overhaul of its business to its purchase of Silicon Valley Bank’s UK arm.

In prepared remarks, Tucker and Quinn each reiterated the board’s recommendation that shareholders vote against a resolution on the docket for its annual general meeting in May that would force the bank to come up with a plan to spin off or reorganize its Asian business — the lender’s main source of profits.

HSBC's biggest shareholder reignites debate about breaking up the bank.

Tucker said the board was unanimous in its opposition to the resolution, stating plainly: “It would not be in your interest to split the bank.”.

He mentioned the board had previously reviewed a range of options for restructuring the bank, and concluded that such alternatives would “materially destroy value for shareholders,” including dividends.

“Our strategy is working,” Tucker told the room of more than 1,000 shareholders. “Our current strategy is moving dividends up.”.

HSBC has been facing calls to separate its Asian business from the rest of the bank over the past year.

Shareholders in Hong Kong — where HSBC is a mainstay of many retail investors’ portfolios — contend that the London-based lender’s performance has been dragged down by its businesses in other regions.

Quinn addressed those complaints head-on Monday, saying “our profits in Hong Kong and the UK are no longer being dragged down by underperformance elsewhere. The group is performing well as a whole.”.

Pressed later by a shareholder on the issue, Quinn said a breakup of the bank would result in “significant revenue loss” because much of its business relied on cross-border transactions.

Investors have also been unhappy with HSBC scrapping its dividend in 2020, at the request of British regulators. They argue that if the lender cordoned off its activities in Asia, it would no longer have to expose Hong Kong shareholders to requests in other jurisdictions.

Christine Fong, a district council member in Hong Kong, remarked she represented about 500 small shareholders who had been affected by the dividend cancellation.

“Street hawkers, taxi drivers or teachers — they all relied on the dividend to pay for their regular expenses, like mortgage, insurance payments, school fees,” Fong told CNN.

“That’s why, three years ago, what HSBC did upset those small minority shareholders.”.

Fong has now joined calls for shareholders to vote in favor of the proposal for the bank to spin off its Asian business, despite the lender bringing back its dividend in 2021, albeit at a lower level.

Ken Lui, an activist shareholder in Hong Kong who put the resolution together, doubled down on his call for support ahead of the meeting Monday.

The resolution will require 75% of votes to be passed in May, but “nothing is impossible,” he told reporters outside the meeting venue.

Lui, who said he personally held a stake worth 100 million Hong Kong dollars ($12.7 million), laid out plans for his team to focus on “targeted outreach to institutional shareholders to present our case and gain their support.”.

His group will also canvass 18 districts of Hong Kong “to tell HSBC shareholders that they finally have a chance to speak for themselves and protect their rights through voting,” he added.

HSBC is also facing pressure from its largest shareholder.

Ping An (PNGAY), China’s biggest insurer, holds an 8% stake in HSBC and has backed calls for the bank to rethink its structure.

In a series of remarks made public by the Chinese firm last November, Huang Yong, chairman of Ping An’s asset management arm, noted “we will support any initiatives including a spinoff that are conducive to improve HSBC’s performance and value.”.

Since then, the insurance giant’s views haven’t changed, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The source told CNN that Ping An has been calling for HSBC to explore a reorganization, with an eye on boosting its valuation and simplifying its regulatory obligations around the globe.

It has been revealed that the insurer has not recommended a specific path forward but will support any initiatives, including a spinoff of its Asian business, that could boost its stock performance or value, the person added. Ping An did not immediately respond to a request for comment on how it planned to vote at the upcoming general meeting.

It has been revealed that HSBC’s leaders were also asked Monfday why the bank had scooped up the British unit of SVB following the stunning collapse of its parent in the United States. The purchase was made for £1 ($1.20) last month, just days after SVB had folded.

Critics have questioned HSBC’s ability to perform adequate due diligence on SVB UK’s customers because of how quickly the deal came together.

According to recent reports, “Did HSBC look into the clients of SVB in detail? Say, the financial statement — whether they can pay back the loan?” said Fong.

HSBC buys SVB's UK business, ending 'nightmare' for British tech.

Quinn and Tucker defended the acquisition, calling it a good business opportunity that allowed the bank to gain hundreds of innovative startups as customers. They pushed back on the notion that management hadn’t had time to carry out proper due diligence.

Tucker also weighed in on recent tumult in the banking industry, saying he did not expect an “immediate impact” on HSBC.

“After the collapse of a number of smaller regional banks and the takeover of Credit Suisse, the share prices of all banks have been suppressed,” he noted.

Recent findings suggest that but he mentioned he did not believe such developments represented “a systemic risk” to the sector. “I do expect a period of uncertainty” before nerves settle, he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Romario was capped 70 times by Brazil.

Few would have predicted that Carlo Ancelotti would be facing the wrath of a Brazil legend just 18 months into his tenure as head coach of the national team.

But Romario, Brazil's fourth-highest scorer behind only Neymar, Pele and Ronaldo, has publicly demanded legendary manager Ancelotti be relieved of his duties twice in the past week.

It all started after Brazil suffered a 3-2 friendly defeat by Japan on Friday thanks to a controversial stoppage-time winner from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto.

Ancelotti received a red card for dissent in the aftermath - the first of his international management career, as Barcelona forward Raphinha also saw red.

And after Brazil's friendly defeat, Romario took to social media to air his frustrations about the former Real Madrid boss.

"Ancelotti, enough is enough! Pack your bags and leave!" he wrote on Instagram.

In a recent development, "Nobody questions your history. You are one of the greatest coaches world football has ever seen, but that was at club level.".

Brazil were eliminated by Norway in the last 16 at the 2026 World Cup, meaning they failed to qualify for the quarter-finals for the first time since 1990.

And Romario alluded to this too, stating the country "can't take the risk of throwing another World Cup in the trash - the time to act is now!".

The Brazil boss has been in the game long enough to know how to deal with all sorts of opinions.

Ancelotti has won the Champions League a record five times as a head coach and won the league title in all of Europe's top five divisions, along with multiple domestic cups.

But his record with Brazil is far from perfect. Across 21 matches, they have recorded 12 wins, four draws and five defeats.

However, while Ancelotti acknowledges the need for improvement, he emphasised the fact that it is still "a newly introduced project".

Speaking before Brazil's friendly with Singapore on Tuesday the Italian said: "In a democratic country with freedom of speech, everyone is allowed to express their opinion.

"It's not up to me to say whether the things he indicates are correct, wrong or just stupid. The truth is that Romario talks a lot. A lot. It's his right.".

Despite the criticism he has faced, Ancelotti feels Brazil are on the right track - and who is to tell him otherwise when you look at his track record?

"I really like what we're doing," he remarked.

You would have thought that would have been enough to let it lie for the time being.

But before Brazil had even kicked a ball in their next friendly against Singapore, Romario was speaking out again.

The former striker, who is the ninth-highest scorer in football history with 784 goals, doubled down on his calls for Ancelotti to be sacked.

"I talk a lot because when it comes to the national team, I have size, weight and power of speech," Romario, 60, stated.

According to recent reports, "I do not speak to gain followers, I do not speak for people to like me. I speak my mind.

"I have worn this shirt for many years and I am pretty sure I was one of the ones that helped the 'little yellow' be respected all over the world.".

He mentioned he respected Ancelotti but added he hadn't "added anything new" to the national side.

Sources indicate that "I will say it again: resign! We will find another coach who will do a better job than you.

"And I'm saying this to your face, not through a message, including to the president of the [Brazilian Football Confederation], who is long overdue to fire you.".

Brazil faced Singapore in their final match of 2026 on Tuesday and won 7-0.

Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior, who has come under scrutiny of his own so far this season, scored a hat-trick within the opening 21 minutes while Bournemouth winger Rayan and Chelsea's Estevao were also on the scoresheet.

That result that may bring a pause to proceedings in this war of words for now.

However, if this past seven days has proved anything, it is that this saga is likely far from over.

Performance-wise, this is one of the fastest laptops on the market no matter how you stack it. The MacBook Pros have fans, so they're better at handling the stress of creative apps and games over longer periods of time.

Industry observers note that the M5 MacBook Air lasted 17 hours and 40 minutes in our battery life benchmark, which is a video rundown test. That's a small downgrade from the last generation, but you won't be screwed if you forget your charger at home.

Like all MacBooks, its build quality is class-leading. You can take your pick from four neutral finishes: sky blue, silver, starlight, and midnight.

For its ultraportable design and slightly lower price tag, I deem the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air the best MacBook for college students — particularly liberal arts, humanities, nursing, and social science majors. In a recent development, the Neo lasts for around 15 hours per charge. It dies much sooner than an Air or Pro, but it'll definitely get you through a full workday with plenty of juice to spare.

But just know that AAA gaming is possible here if you want to run the occasional mission after work.

Design-wise, the M6 MacBook Pro is slightly less portable than the Air, but not by much. It's less than 0.2 inches thicker than both sizes and 0.1 pounds heavier than the 15-inch model. I've tested dozens of laptops over the course of my career, and none of them sound better than a MacBook Pro.

Recent findings suggest that the M5 MacBook Pro looks as spectacular as it sounds, as per tradition. (Apple hasn't made any drastic design changes to it since 2021.) Compared to the M5 MacBook Air's standard Liquid Retina screen, its mini-LED "Liquid Retina XDR" display is crisper, brighter, and smoother when displaying visuals in motion. Take your pick from two finishes: space black or silver. Be mindful that the former is a fingerprint magnet.

We haven't run our battery life test on the M6 MacBook Pro yet, but we have high expectations. Last year's M5 model held out for 21 hours and 17 minutes to become the longest-lasting MacBook we've ever tried.

In a recent development, apple's all-fresh MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is geared toward deep-pocketed creative professionals whose work requires a ton of horsepower and a reference-quality display. Its name is a mouthful, and its screen is an eyeful. Apple's all-newly introduced MacBook Pro has an elite tandem OLED display that wowed Mashable Tech Editor Timothy Beck Werth. ("Reference-quality" refers to the fact that its colors are extremely lifelike and accurate.) It's an absolutely luscious display — not to mention super bright. It can hit up to 2,000 nits of peak HDR brightness, which makes it one of the brightest laptop displays ever made.

It has been revealed that the new MacBook Pro's OLED display has touch capabilities, too, which is mainly interesting because it brings support for the Dynamic Island instead of a webcam notch. Compared to the M6 chip in the fresh base MacBook Pro, it offers a jaw-dropping 57 percent performance boost when running intensive software.

It has been revealed that what's even more impressive is the fact that the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display doesn't heat up easily, despite being thinner and lighter than the standard MacBook Pros. The 16-inch model weighs in at four pounds — a whopping 0.7 pounds less than its non-OLED counterpart, which makes a real difference when you're working on the go.

It has been revealed that the other main design differences between this model and the standard MacBook Pro are its glowing Apple logo and upgraded sound system, which "[provides] deeper bass and better clarity," Werth remarked. Their keyboards, trackpads, color options, webcams, mics, and port setups are the same.

Our battery life test results for the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display aren't finalized yet, but Apple rated it at up to 24 hours of video streaming (same as the regular Pro).

In November 2026, I added two newly introduced picks based on our latest round of testing. The M6 MacBook Pro is now our upgrade pick, and the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is our new top pick for professional creatives. (Look for their battery life test results in the next upgrade.) I also added information about Black Friday MacBook deals.

In August 2026, I updated this guide to reflect Apple's newly increased MacBook prices and named the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air our top pick for college students.

Sources indicate that in May 2026, I added the results of our battery life testing for the M5 MacBook Air. It was able to loop a video for 17 hours and 40 minutes before dying.

Industry observers note that macBooks tend to go on sale at their deepest discounts during Amazon's summer Prime Day sale and around Black Friday. They also see steep price cuts as soon as they're no longer current-generation models, meaning right after Apple announces their successors (which usually happens every year in March and October.).

Recent findings suggest that apple hosts a Black Friday sale every year, but it just entails free gift card promotions. For proper price cuts, shop around at third-party retailers like Amazon and Best Buy.

It has been revealed that first, a little info about how Apple classifies its older products. Devices that it stopped selling more than five years ago but less than seven are considered "vintage," whereas devices it stopped selling more than seven years ago are "obsolete.".

In a recent development, vintage MacBooks are still eligible for hardware support from Apple, depending on parts availability, but it won't fix obsolete MacBooks. And you can't get parts for them from third-party service providers like Best Buy and Micro Center.

Recent findings suggest that if your obsolete MacBook is still chugging along like normal, is in good condition, and doesn't seem sluggish or scant on storage, by all means, keep using it. However, if any component breaks, deteriorates, or no longer meets your needs, it's time to send it off to the great MacBook farm in the sky. Consider recycling or donating it so it doesn't sit in a landfill.

It has been revealed that while MacBooks don't get software updates forever, it's not a dealbreaker if yours can't run the latest version of macOS. You might be able to repurpose it as a streaming device or turn it into a Chromebook. That said, a MacBook you use as your primary laptop for school or work needs to be compatible with the current macOS in order to stay secure and continue running Apple apps.

Industry observers note that FYI: The latest version of Apple's Mac operating system, macOS 27 (aka macOS Golden Gate), only works with M-series MacBooks from 2020 or later. That means if your daily driver is an older model with an Intel chip, it's high time to upgrade. It will still get security updates for the next two-ish years but won't support any latest features going forward.

Some of the best Windows laptops and Chromebooks we've tested can rival MacBooks on performance and/or build quality. My favorite MacBook alternatives include the Asus Zenbook A14, the Dell XPS 13, and the Dell XPS 14.

If you want to stay within the Apple ecosystem, iPads also make good MacBook alternatives thanks to iPadOS's "windowing" system.

Industry observers note that mashable has been writing about laptops for over a decade, and I've personally been covering them since 2023. I also helped develop the rigorous hands-on testing process we currently use to review them. This methodology revolves around four criteria:.

The laptops we review get put to work as our primary computers. This includes trying any unique software or use cases they support. We also subject all of our loaners to a multi-app/tab stress test and Primate Labs' Geekbench, which measures CPU performance in common tasks. Gaming laptops get put through additional graphical benchmarking.

According to recent reports, to gauge a laptop's stamina, we conduct a battery rundown test that involves playing a looped 1080p version of "Tears of Steel," a short open-source Blender movie, at 50 percent brightness and 50 percent volume. Ideally, we hope to get at least 19 hours of battery life from MacBooks.

Recent findings suggest that as we're using a laptop, we zero in on certain components to evaluate its build quality. These include the display, keyboard, touchpad, webcam, speakers, and ports. We also assess its overall aesthetic and portability.

Sources indicate that we determine the ultimate value of a laptop by comparing its performance, design/build quality, and battery life to other laptops with similar pricing, specs, release dates, and use cases. We consider any accessories it comes with, any upgrades from its predecessor(s), and its future-proofing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that 1Password has long been one of our favorite password managers. We rated it an 8/10 in WIRED Reviews, in part because it's been around for decades and still manages to stay on the cutting edge of keeping your logins safe. It's our upgrade pick for all the extra features it offers compared to other password managers. 1Password has apps that work just about everywhere, including on macOS, iOS, Android, Windows, Linux, and ChromeOS. There are plug-ins for your favorite web browser too, which makes it easy to generate and edit new passwords on the fly.

There are also some very nice features in 1Password that you won't find elsewhere. If you frequently travel across national borders, you’ll appreciate Travel Mode. This mode lets you delete any sensitive data from your devices before you travel and then restore it with a click after you’ve crossed a border. This prevents anyone, including law enforcement at international borders, from accessing your complete password vault. In addition to being a password manager, 1Password can act as an authentication app like Google Authenticator, and for added security, it creates a secret key to the encryption key it uses, meaning no one can decrypt your passwords without that key.

Industry observers note that 1Password also offers tight integration with other mobile apps. Rather than needing to copy and paste passwords from your password manager to other apps (which puts your password on the clipboard at least for a moment), 1Password is integrated with many apps and can autofill. This is more noticeable on iOS, where inter-app communication is more restricted. You can get savings on the tech giant’s suite of products with our 1Password coupons and deals.

Danny Kelly obituary

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (916 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ebullient journalist, magazine editor and broadcaster whose passion for music and football shone through all his work.
  • In a recent development, danny Kelly, who has died aged 69, influenced music journalism and sports broadcasting for more than four decades.
  • Sources indicate that in 1997 Kelly helped set up Football 365, one of the earliest football websites, and still one of the most popular in the UK.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ebullient journalist, magazine editor and broadcaster whose passion for music and football shone through all his work.

In a recent development, danny Kelly, who has died aged 69, influenced music journalism and sports broadcasting for more than four decades. Humour, enthusiasm and encyclopedic knowledge were the hallmarks of his work as a writer and editor at the New Musical Express (NME) and Q magazine, and throughout his online, TV and audio career, most prominently around his passion for football.

Sources indicate that in 1997 Kelly helped set up Football 365, one of the earliest football websites, and still one of the most popular in the UK. He hosted radio demonstrates on BBC 5 Live, TalkSport, BT Sport and Times Radio, as well as many podcasts including The View from the Lane, about the team he had supported since childhood, Tottenham Hotspur.

Industry observers note that kelly’s deputy at the NME, Stuart Maconie, described how he championed “the best of everything … roots, rock, reggae, the Smiths, Tamla Motown, the Clash, T.Rex, prog”. His close friend Danny Baker, his regular co-host since 1992, remarked that they shared “music, football, life … an absurd private universe of turmoil” together and turned to humour “to forge another path for football punditry, based in hoopla, voodoo and toasters”.

Sources indicate that kelly’s much-shared 2008 commentary of an Arsenal and Spurs match, alongside the retired footballer Stan Collymore, exemplified his relatable passion: “I love football, Stan! I love it!” he shouted when Spurs equalised, adding, seconds later, “How unprofessional.” Collymore described how Kelly brought him to TalkSport after he struggled with chronic mental health issues; Kelly gave many others support during their own physical and psychological struggles.

Born in London, into a family that had recently emigrated from County Carlow in Ireland to Islington, Danny was the oldest of the six children of Josie (nee Martin), a school dinner lady, and Andy, a railway worker.

Despite growing up “literally in the shadow of Highbury Stadium”, and in a family of Arsenal supporters, Danny supported their near-rivals. Speaking to FourFourTwo magazine in 2006, he mentioned that Spurs represented “the true spirit of rock’n’roll”.

A pupil at Sacred Heart primary school in Holloway and later at St Aloysius’ College in Highgate, Kelly loved history (“but I don’t suppose anyone really cares about my opinions about the Anglo-Prussian agreements of the 17th century,” he told the Upcoming York Times’ sports website The Athletic in 2022).

In a 2020 interview with the Behind the Lines podcast, he described himself as “teenage music fanatic”, calling the NME in the mid-1970s his “bible”.

After failing to complete law and combined arts studies at Leicester University through “lack of effort, and punk rock”, he worked at British Rail on the complaints counter and as a station announcer. As a shop steward with the Transport Salaried Staffs’ Association, he wrote about music in the union magazine. A copy picked up by the NME jazz critic Richard Cook at a TUC conference in 1983 led to freelance work for Kelly, who then returned to college to pursue media studies at the Polytechnic of Central London (now the University of Westminster).

His writing was ebullient and vivid: Marvin Gaye possessed “a combination of gifts seldom stuffed into one body, one psyche”; the Smiths made “a Catherine wheel of inspired language” against “shifting, sometimes unnervingly evocative and beautiful guitar music”. Joining the NME in 1985 as a writer, he became deputy editor in 1987 and editor in 1990, before taking over Q in 1992.

There, he commanded audiences in the office and at after-work pub sessions regaling his stories of meeting musicians, and presented serious cover stars with characteristic irreverence: Sting, formerly of the Police, in handcuffs; Kate Bush under the headline “Booze, fags, blokes and me”.

In 1995, he launched Total Sport magazine, which ran for four years, and from 1997 to 1998 presented the late-night Channel 4 sports and entertainment show Under the Moon. Simultaneously, he ran editorial operations for Football 365, which became popular during the 1998 World Cup.

His subsequent radio career was prolific and popular. On TalkSport’s This Sporting Life, his interviewees included Virginia Wade, Frank Bruno and Eric Bristow. Trans Euro Express combined his love of European football and music, while his expertise in other sports, including cycling and American football, was in regular demand.

It has been revealed that A year-long marriage ended in 1998; in 2005, the literary journalist and editor Alex Clark became his partner. He married her, wearing shoes from a range by his favourite rapper, MF Doom, in 2021. They moved to Kilkenny in 2018 to be near his mother, who had returned to Ireland.

It has been revealed that kelly broadcast remotely throughout the pandemic, up until his diagnosis with oesophageal cancer in March. He posted a diary of his treatment, the Kelly Cancer Kronikles, to his 106,000 followers on X until August, its title referencing one of his literary heroes, the fictional schoolboy Nigel Molesworth.

“I hope that what I’ve done over the years is to be honest and open about football, life, culture, everything else,” he remarked to the Athletic, and added the only two pieces of advice he ever gave to aspiring broadcasters. “Be a version of yourself, but add an extra 15% of personality. And don’t be shit. Try not to be shit and you’ll be OK.”.

Alex, his mother, Josie, and his siblings, Margaret, Michael, Andrew, Joanna and John, survive him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Baker featured in five Premier League games for Brighton in the 2023-24 season.

Millwall are undertaking disciplinary proceedings against forward Benicio Baker following social media posts critical of senior figures at the club, BBC Sport understands.

The 22-year-old winger has played only for the Lions' under-21 side since joining from Brighton in February 2025 on a long-term deal.

BBC Sport understands the proceedings relate to a number of off-field matters, including social media activity.

Posts attributed to Baker's account, which has since been deactivated on Instagram but has been widely republished, appeared critical of senior figures at Millwall and suggested he "can't even train with the (under) 21s".

It is understood Baker was initially unavailable because of injury, but he is now the subject of disciplinary proceedings which, in the most serious circumstances, could lead to the cancellation of his contract.

Baker is also understood to be exploring options away from Millwall.

At the height of his career, Baker made six first-team appearances for Brighton under former manager Roberto de Zerbi, including in the Premier League.

The England Under-20 international also spent time in the academy systems at West Ham and Porto before making 14 senior appearances on loan as Port Vale finished second in League Two in 2024.

While at West Ham, before joining Porto, he was linked with moves to overseas clubs including Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Benfica.

Millwall have declined to comment, while representatives for Baker have been contacted.

NASA reveals bold new proposal to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA has revealed new details about its accelerated effort to return American astronauts to the Moon in 2028.
  • During an October 23 briefing, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and other agency leaders outlined the next steps for the Artemis program.
  • The announcement builds on priorities introduced earlier this year through NASA's Ignition initiative.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA has revealed new details about its accelerated effort to return American astronauts to the Moon in 2028. The updated strategy includes testing two competing lunar landers, streamlining rocket preparations, and introducing a lighter spacesuit to help make the first moonwalks possible sooner.

During an October 23 briefing, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and other agency leaders outlined the next steps for the Artemis program. The revised approach centers on two major missions: Artemis III, a test flight scheduled for 2027, and Artemis IV, which is intended to land astronauts on the lunar surface in 2028.

The announcement builds on priorities introduced earlier this year through NASA's Ignition initiative. Agency officials also highlighted recent progress in spacecraft development, mission preparations, and partnerships with private aerospace companies. These efforts are intended to reduce technical risks, accelerate the schedule, and establish the foundation for a lasting American presence on the Moon.

"This is a very energized NASA, and these updates are only a small part of that story. We are bringing extreme focus to the mission to ensure delivery of world-changing outcomes as swiftly, safely, affordably, and successfully as possible," said Isaacman. "NASA is driving outcomes to make Moon missions a reality, and we're not waiting for others to bring their intends to us -- the campaign must move with urgency as strategic competitors pursue a permanent presence beyond Earth.".

Artemis III Will Test Two Lunar Landers in Earth Orbit.

Before attempting another crewed Moon landing, NASA looks to conduct a major rehearsal in Earth orbit. The Artemis III mission will bring together NASA's Orion spacecraft and experimental lunar landers developed by SpaceX and Blue Origin.

Four astronauts will travel aboard Orion, launching on NASA's powerful SLS (Space Launch System) rocket. During the planned 14-day mission, the crew will practice rendezvous and docking procedures with both companies' lander test vehicles. Rendezvous involves guiding two spacecraft to meet in orbit, while docking allows them to connect so astronauts can move between vehicles.

These demonstrations are designed to verify key spacecraft capabilities before Artemis IV attempts to carry astronauts to the Moon's surface.

The tests will take place in a carefully planned sequence. Blue Origin will first launch a test version of its Blue Moon lander into Earth orbit. NASA will then send Orion and its four astronauts into space aboard the SLS rocket, where Orion will rendezvous and dock with the Blue Moon vehicle.

Next, SpaceX will launch a test version of its Version 3 Starship lunar lander. Orion will separate from Blue Moon and perform another docking maneuver, this time with Starship. By testing both systems during a single crewed mission, NASA aims to gather essential operational experience while reducing uncertainties before the 2028 landing attempt.

NASA Cuts Rocket Preparation Times and Costs.

Industry observers note that the fresh mission details follow other recent Artemis progress reports. According to NASA, the hardware needed for Artemis III remains on schedule, and improvements in processing have reduced preparation timelines by approximately 50%.

The agency also reported a significant engineering achievement involving a critical rocket fuel-line component. Rather than relying on an outside supplier, NASA engineers redesigned, manufactured, and tested the component themselves in just five months. The work cost roughly one-tenth of an earlier estimate from an external vendor.

Sources indicate that "NASA should be expected to do this kind of work, and we have some of the best technical knowledge in the world on rocket hardware and operations to do it," noted Jeremy Parsons, the agency's Artemis program manager. "It's an example of how we are rebuilding our core competencies and developing centers of excellence in technical functions instead of continuing to outsource expertise.".

The improvements reflect NASA's broader effort to strengthen its internal engineering capabilities, shorten development schedules, and reduce the cost of preparing missions for launch.

SpaceX and Blue Origin Offer Different Paths to the Moon.

Industry observers note that for Artemis IV in 2028, NASA intends to launch astronauts aboard Orion using the SLS rocket from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Once in space, the crew will rely on a lunar landing system developed by either SpaceX or Blue Origin to reach the Moon's surface.

Both companies have revised their original mission designs to make operations simpler, more efficient, and more adaptable. Although they share the same objective, their approaches to transporting astronauts to the lunar surface differ considerably.

Sources indicate that spaceX looks to use its Starship spacecraft, which will take on additional propellant while orbiting Earth. After refueling, Starship will meet Orion and carry the spacecraft toward the Moon. Refueling in orbit is an notable part of SpaceX's strategy because it allows the vehicle to receive the propellant needed for its journey after leaving the launchpad.

Sources indicate that blue Origin is developing a different approach using its Blue Moon Mark 2 lander. Its proposal calls for additional propulsion stages in Earth orbit to send the lander toward the Moon. The lander will then meet Orion in a relatively low lunar orbit before carrying astronauts down to the surface.

Industry observers note that both companies are working toward having their systems ready to support a crewed Moon landing in 2028. Maintaining two potential landing systems gives NASA greater flexibility as development and testing continue.

NASA Explores New Rocket Options for Artemis IV.

NASA is also considering two possible upper stages for the SLS rocket used on Artemis IV. An upper stage is the portion of a rocket that provides additional propulsion after the earlier stages have completed their work, helping send a spacecraft toward its destination.

One option is the interim cryogenic propulsion stage already used by SLS. The other is an extended version of United Launch Alliance's Centaur V upper stage, which would hold additional propellant.

According to recent reports, by developing both possibilities, NASA hopes to preserve flexibility in its launch plans and avoid becoming dependent on a single technical solution. Having alternatives could help the agency respond to engineering challenges without jeopardizing the broader Moon landing schedule.

A Newly introduced Lightweight Spacesuit Could Speed Up Moonwalks.

Another notable change involves the spacesuits astronauts will wear while exploring the lunar surface.

NASA is working with Axiom Space on a second, lighter design known as the "Sortie suit." The fresh suit is intended specifically for the first Moon surface excursions and weighs approximately half as much as Axiom's larger primary spacesuit.

The lighter design could simplify preparations for the earliest landing missions and help astronauts begin exploring the lunar surface sooner.

According to recent reports, however, the Sortie suit is not intended to replace the primary design. Axiom's more capable suit will remain part of NASA's prepares for future missions that require longer periods outside the spacecraft and more demanding surface activities.

Building a Permanent Human Presence on the Moon.

NASA's ambitions extend well beyond returning astronauts to the lunar surface for a single mission.

It has been revealed that as the Artemis program advances, the agency intends to send crews on increasingly challenging expeditions near the Moon's South Pole. This region is an important focus of future lunar exploration, and the missions are designed to expand how much of the Moon humans can investigate directly.

NASA describes the effort as part of a latest Golden Age of innovation and exploration. The agency expects its lunar missions to support scientific discoveries, generate economic benefits, and encourage the development of technologies needed for more ambitious space exploration.

Ultimately, the goal is to establish an enduring human presence on the Moon rather than repeat the brief visits of earlier lunar expeditions. The experience gained from operating spacecraft, supporting astronauts, and carrying out increasingly complex missions on the lunar surface will also help NASA prepare for another historic objective: sending the first astronauts to Mars.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job.

The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments.

There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the 4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows.

Recent findings suggest that pocognoli’s team scored five goals in six Nations League games, four coming against North Macedonia. They drew blanks in three fixtures. The concession of 10 depicts a team soft against set pieces and in open play. Scotland have wingers who are not appropriately deployed because of dedication to a system. They have an obvious shortage of centre-backs yet Pocognoli picks three at a time. The midfield lacks balance. Not one player under Pocognoli’s watch is consistently excelling.

Sources indicate that pocognoli is obstinate in respect of his tactics. At club level this can work owing to daily work on a training pitch. Scotland are wedded to a 3-4-2-1 that fits too few of their players. There is no transfer window capacity to change that. Pocognoli’s insistence upon his “philosophy” sets off alarm bells. Although his English is strong, it is far from perfect, which raises questions about communication. Scotland do not look well drilled or clear in approach, which was plain in the unimpressive home win against North Macedonia even before the Switzerland debacle.

Unlike with Clarke, there is no detailed body of work to suggest Pocognoli can adapt or oversee improvement. He achieved great success in Belgium, winning the title at Union Saint-Gilloise, before a brief spell at Monaco. The Scottish FA’s deep faith in this 39-year-old, amid all manner of waffle about metrics and analytics, was on the basis of just over 100 games as a manager. It remains probable that the association erred in not sourcing a coach with dugout experience at a country of similar scale to Scotland. This always had the whiff of trying to be too smart by half.

Recent findings suggest that the best Scotland sides are unapologetically horrible to play against, physical, energetic and direct. Shortcomings in skill are offset by attitude. Pocognoli’s version is the opposite on all fronts, ponderous and timid. The Tartan Army, hardly a ferociously demanding lot, have failed to demonstrate any excitement about Pocognoli.

This counts as no ode to Clarke. After seven years, change was required. It was the turn taken by the Scottish FA in implementing a upcoming strategy that looks increasingly dubious.

Footballers are typically selfish beings. For now it suits the Scotland squad – and is fair – to state Pocognoli requires time and that they are behind him. Not only did the body language amid the unravelling in St Gallen suggest otherwise, those players are likely to adopt a different position if focus turns towards them. Scotland’s contingent is heavy on influential, experienced players.

In a recent development, there is no sense of the Scottish FA dispensing with Pocognoli at this point. Not only would such a move be premature, it would deliver an admission of failure that those running the governing body are never keen on providing. They enjoy the trappings and profile provided by the national team without anything like the adjacent accountability. They are assisted in this context by domestic football obsession within the country. There will be grumblings about Pocognoli for a brief period this week before the theme is placed into cold storage.

Sources indicate that next month’s Uefa 2028 qualifying draw, where Scotland will appear from pot three, carries intrigue and danger for Pocognoli. The assumption that Scotland will feature in the tournament is undermined by performances; England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland are co-hosting and a maximum of two spots are open for any of those nations who do not qualify. Not playing in a competition where games will be staged in Glasgow would count as a humiliation for the Scottish FA.

It has been revealed that if Scotland face competitive games rather than friendlies in March, which will be determined after the draw, Pocognoli needs stark improvement. Without it, his paymasters would then have a decision to make while looking to keep Euro 2028 dreams alive. The situation is already that acute.

Pocognoli was not part of the Scotland party that landed in Glasgow from Zurich on Tuesday. His family have remained in Belgium. Alone with his thoughts on his journey home, Pocognoli must have pondered the harshness of his latest environment. He has the sternest of challenges to quieten legitimate background noise.
